name: Morning Again
label: Revelation
lede: Morning Again went through two singers and a future New Found Glory guitarist in its first year, signed to Revelation, made one album and broke up four months after it came out. The vegan straight edge band from Cooper City, Florida kept coming back anyway.

eras.title: A second band for Culture's guitarist
eras.text: John Wylie of Culture started Morning Again in Cooper City, Florida, and the two bands traded members constantly. Year one brought a demo, a 12" about AOL and child abduction, a tour, two firings and a new singer from Ohio.

years.h: Culture's guitarist starts a second band in Cooper City, Florida
years.p: John Wylie forms Morning Again with singer [[Damien Moyal|b655a47c-28f5-466d-aba1-4d607e4f598a]], guitarist Michael Wolz, bassist Eric Ervin and drummer Louie Long. Straight edge, vegan, anti-religious, anti-government.

years.h: The Cleanest War worries about America Online in 1996
years.p: Five songs cut in January at Studio 13 in Deerfield Beach with Jeremy Staska, out on Conquer the World. America On Line warns about internet dependency and surveillance.
years.xp:
Minus One was inspired by the abduction and murder of Adam Walsh. Remedy imagines authorities sitting on a cure, after the film Outbreak.

According to Wikipedia, reviewers liked Moyal's delivery but found the internet song obscure at the time. A demo tape had come out February 9, and the vinyl lagged the CD by months.

years.cap: Damien Moyal and John Wylie at Cheers, Coconut Grove, Florida, June 11, 1996
years.h: Cheers, Coconut Grove, closes the first tour
years.p: The first North American run goes May 27 to June 12, 1996, and the June 11 date at Cheers is one of its last.

years.cap: Michael Wolz, Eric Ervin and John Wylie at Cheers, Coconut Grove, June 11, 1996
years.h: Moyal and Ervin are out as soon as the tour ends
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Wylie's band fires singer Damien Moyal and bassist Eric Ervin over creative conflicts. Moyal later fronts [[As Friends Rust|2f106f2f-5990-4f50-9590-3fa8da941f98]].

years.h: Future New Found Glory guitarist Chad Gilbert plays bass for a spell
years.p: Wikipedia lists [[Chad Gilbert|4ed8c877-0036-44c7-bf6f-4c9c8e8ccedb]], later of [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]], as Morning Again's bassist for part of 1996. He is one of several players through the lineup that year.

years.cap: Gerardo Villarroel, Kevin Byers and John Wylie at Headquarters, Buffalo, New York, March 5, 1997
years.src: No Echo: Kevin Byers interview · Wikipedia: Morning Again
years.h: Kevin Byers lands in Florida with eighty dollars
years.p: Wylie meets Byers at an Outcast show in Dayton, Ohio, and asks what he'll do next. Byers thinks he's being offered bass. It's the singer's job.
years.xp:
"I thought he was asking me to play bass at first," Byers says. He took a one-way ticket to Florida with "80 dollars cash and the rest of my life in a duffle bag."

Wikipedia puts the change at Byers replacing Moyal after tension between Moyal and Wylie.

years.h: Intention and Moo Cow each get a 7" from the band
years.p: A self-titled 7" comes out on Intention Records, and a split 7" with Shoulder on Moo Cow Records.

eras.title: Eleven months on the road, then the van gave out
eras.text: With Kevin Byers out front, Morning Again toured the US and Europe alongside Converge and Agnostic Front. Revelation signed them, the album came out, and the band was gone by October.

yt: Full set at Club Q, Davie, Florida, 1997
years.h: Matthew Thomas takes the drum stool from Louie Long
years.p: Original drummer Louie Long leaves Morning Again in April 1997, and Matthew Thomas steps in.

yt: God Framed Me live, Dilsen, Belgium, 1997
years.h: Martyr arrives on Belgium's Good Life
years.p: The 12" is Morning Again's first record for the label. The same year brings the My Statement of Life in a Dying World 7" on Immigrant Sun and the Hand of Hope collection.

years.cap: John Wylie and Kevin Byers at Headquarters, Buffalo, New York, March 5, 1997
years.h: Eleven months of touring, from Syracuse to the Netherlands
years.p: From November 1997 to October 1998 Morning Again play the US and Europe with bands including [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]], with Syracuse Hardcore Fest and dates in Germany and the Netherlands.

years.cap: Kevin Byers at Headquarters, Buffalo, New York, March 5, 1997
years.h: Kevin Byers records the Revelation album barely able to speak
years.p: Morning Again cut As Tradition Dies Slowly in twelve days, February 1 to 12, at Studio 13. Byers was sick the whole way through.
years.xp: "I was not feeling well and had a sore throat and could barely speak through most of it," Byers says. On the record, "you can hear my voice slowly burn out."

years.h: Joseph Simmons is fired; Stephen Looker gets the credit
years.p: Simmons plays guitar on As Tradition Dies Slowly and is fired three weeks later. Looker replaces him and is credited on an album he didn't play on.

years.src: Wikipedia: As Tradition Dies Slowly · No Echo
years.h: Revelation releases As Tradition Dies Slowly
years.p: Seven new songs and three re-recordings, with art by [[Richie Birkenhead|7a1a6273-c31b-4828-8e20-0d6ea66943aa]] of [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]]. It spends nine weeks on CMJ's Loud Rock chart and peaks at No. 22.
years.xp:
Jeremy Staska produced it and Alan Douches mastered it. It was the band's first release to chart at all, including No. 50 on FMQB's Metal Detector.

"Rev just felt right for us," Byers says, after someone doing A&R for Revelation approached the band.

years.big: We were burnt out on touring and each other.
years.src: No Echo: Kevin Byers interview · Wikipedia: Morning Again
years.h: Morning Again split and skip CMJ
years.p: Kevin Byers on the October 1998 breakup, four months after the album. The band cancels its CMJ Music Marathon slot.
years.xp:
Byers adds that a van broke down on the way to the first show of a US tour, and "we were so broke we couldn't even finish it." He had also moved home to care for his newborn daughter.

Wylie was being pulled toward other projects, including his label Eulogy Recordings and the band Where Fear and Weapons Meet.

Earlier that year the band also put out a split with [[25 ta Life|7be13e13-6362-4e97-aca7-edf7908cbeab]] on Good Life and the To Die a Bitter Death 7" on Immigrant Sun.

eras.title: Reunions under other names
eras.text: Morning Again kept coming back for one-offs, sometimes billed as the name of an old record. Wylie's label, Eulogy, kept the catalog in print.

years.h: Moyal returns, billed as Cleanest War
years.p: Morning Again reunite with their fired first singer, Damien Moyal, and play under the name of their first record.

years.h: The Fallen... The Few That Remain comes out on Eulogy
years.p: A Morning Again collection on John Wylie's own label, Eulogy Recordings.

years.h: An Orlando reunion billed as Hand of Hope
years.p: Morning Again play Orlando under the name of their 1997 collection, with Moyal and Ervin back. Hand of the Martyr later gathers the early records on Alveran and Eulogy.

eras.title: Festivals in Belgium and Japan, new songs on Revelation
eras.text: Kevin Byers and Damien Moyal took turns out front as Morning Again became a festival band in Europe and Japan. Twenty years after the album, Revelation put out new songs.

years.h: Groezrock puts the band on a big European stage again
years.p: Kevin Byers fronts Morning Again at Belgium's Groezrock festival on April 22, 2011, the first big stage of the reunion years.

years.h: Two singers in one year, from Ieperfest to Tokyo
years.p: Damien Moyal sings at Ieperfest in Belgium. Kevin Byers takes Morning Again to Japan for the Bloodaxe festival in Tokyo and a show in Nagoya.

yt: hate5six full set, This Is Hardcore, July 23, 2015
years.h: Philadelphia's This Is Hardcore, then vinyl
years.p: Morning Again play This Is Hardcore in July. Revelation re-presses As Tradition Dies Slowly on vinyl the same month.

years.h: After 20 years, a new EP
years.p: Survival Instinct is written by email and text across state lines and comes out November 9 on Revelation, twenty years after As Tradition Dies Slowly.

eras.title: Select shows and borrowed time
eras.text: Morning Again moved to select shows and short tours instead of long runs, and the first singer came back when the current one couldn't make the trip.

years.cap: Eric Ervin, Kevin Byers and John Wylie at Ieperfest, Ypres, Belgium, July 2, 2022
years.h: A second Revelation EP, then Ieperfest in Ypres
years.p: Borrowed Time follows on Revelation, and a European tour includes Ieperfest on July 2.

yt: hate5six full set, This Is Hardcore 2024
years.h: Damien Moyal fills in when Kevin Byers hurts his shoulder
years.p: With Byers out for the European tour, Morning Again's first singer takes his place.

sources.title: No Echo: Morning Again to return with new EP on Revelation
